title: Platform systems & services: runbooks, dashboards, alerts, roadmap, retrospective (2026 Q1)
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

This document is the canonical reference for Platform Systems & Services operational runbooks, dashboards and alerting patterns, and the Q1 2026 roadmap and retrospective. It is intended for oncall engineers, platform maintainers, and product stakeholders who rely on predictable platform uptime and economical inference serving.

Sections included below: scope, system inventory, dashboards & panels, alerting thresholds and example rules, standard incident runbooks, retrospective highlights from Q1 2026, roadmap items for Q2–Q3 2026, ownership and run cadence, and appendices with commands and links.

Scope

- Systems in scope: API gateway, request router (smart-routing), serving runtime (GPU pools), KV/prefix cache, batch scheduler, metrics/logging stack (Prometheus / Thanos / Grafana / Loki), deployment pipelines (CI/CD), and control plane services (model catalog, rollout manager).
- This doc covers production and dedicated environments; private deployments have a subset of runbooks referenced in the onprem packaging playbook.

1) Systems & Services Inventory (summary)

- api-gateway (service): ingress, auth, rate-limiting. Primary SLO: 99.95% 1m request success. Owner: api-team.
- request-router (service): routes requests to appropriate model variant / region. Primary SLO: 99.9% request routing latency < 50ms. Owner: serving-routing.
- serving-runtime (service): GPU inference engine, KV cache integration, autoscaling. Primary SLO: 99.9% token generation availability; p50 latency targets depend on model class (see performance-standards). Owner: serving-runtime.
- kv-cache (service): Redis/cluster for prefix/KV caching. SLO: 99.99% availability. Owner: infra-platform.
- batch-scheduler (service): groups short requests for throughput; SLO: 99.9% successful batch execution. Owner: serving-runtime.
- metrics-stack: Prometheus + Thanos (long term), Grafana dashboards, Alertmanager. Owner: eng-platform observability.

2) Dashboards & Alerts: recommended panels and thresholds

High-level dashboard layout (minimum):
- Overview (global health): request rate, error rate, p50/p95/p99 latency (serving), GPU utilization (per-pool), queue depth, prefix cache hit rate, cost-per-token estimate.
- Per-service: detailed latency histograms, downstream errors, retry counts, circuit breaker state.
- Autoscaling: active replicas, scale events, cooldowns, CPU/GPU pressure.
- Infrastructure: node health, disk pressure, network packet drops, Prometheus target status.

Key metrics and recommended thresholds: (these are starting defaults; tune per-customer/region)
- request_rate_total (per-second) — no alert by default; used for capacity spikes.
- http_request_errors_total / http_requests_total (error ratio) — Alert: if errors > 1% for 5m AND absolute errors > 50/min -> SEV2.
- serving_latency_seconds_bucket (p99) — Alert: if p99 > 1.5x target for 10m -> SEV2; if p99 > 3x target for 5m -> SEV1.
- gpu_utilization_percent (per-pool) — Alert: > 95% sustained for 15m -> capacity pressure (SEV2); > 99% for 5m -> SEV1 and consider autoscale/burst.
- kv_cache_hit_rate_percent — Alert: < 75% for 10m -> investigate cache eviction/regeneration (SEV3).
- queue_depth (per-pool) — Alert: > 500 requests queued for 5m -> SEV2.
- prometheus_target_up == 0 for >3m -> ops-notify (SEV3).

Example Prometheus alert (adapt to local naming):

ALERT HighGatewayErrorRate
  IF sum(rate(http_requests_total{service=\"api-gateway\",code!~\"2..\"}[5m])) by (instance) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{service=\"api-gateway\"}[5m])) by (instance) > 0.01
  AND sum(rate(http_requests_total{service=\"api-gateway\"}[5m])) by (instance) > 0.8
  FOR 5m
  LABELS { severity = \"page\" }
  ANNOTATIONS {
    summary = \"High error rate on api-gateway ({{ $labels.instance }})\",
    runbook = \"/confluence/eng-platform/platform-systems-services-runbooks-dashboards-alerts-roadmap-retrospective-2026-q1.json#runbook--api-gateway-error-spike\"
  }

Grafana panel examples (queries)
- p99 latency: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(serving_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model_variant))
- GPU utilization: avg_over_time(gpu_utilization_percent{pool=\"general\"}[5m])
- Cache hit rate: sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / (sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) + sum(rate(kv_cache_misses_total[5m])))

3) Standard incident runbooks (short, actionable)

Runbook: API Gateway error spike
- Severity: SEV2/SEV1 depending on error ratio and customer impact.
- Pager: api-gateway oncall.
- Steps:
  1) Verify alert and scope: use Grafana Overview to check which regions/instances are affected.
  2) Identify error types: check logs in Loki and trace IDs from X-Request-ID. Common causes: auth token expiry, rate limit misconfig, dependency timeouts.
  3) If rate limiting misconfiguration, temporarily relax limits via admin API: curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/ratelimit/override -d '{\"scope\":\"global\",\"qps\":2000}' 
  4) If downstream dependency failure, enable fail-open policy on gateway to bypass non-critical checks (short term).
  5) If configuration deployment triggered the issue, rollback via CI: circleci jobs -> revert last deploy -> kubectl rollout undo deployment/api-gateway.
  6) Post-incident: capture root cause, add new test to CI that reproduces failure mode, and update dashboards.

Runbook: Serving runtime high p99 latency
- Severity: SEV2/SEV1. Pager: serving-runtime oncall.
- Steps:
  1) Confirm alert: check p99 by model_variant. Identify if a single model or all models are impacted.
  2) Check GPU pool saturation, queue depth, and batch sizes.
  3) If GPU utilization > 95% and queue depth high: scale up pool (if autoscale disabled) or enable burst capacity: POST /internal/autoscale/pools/{pool}/burst
  4) If only some requests affected: apply fast fallback to a lower-latency model variant via rollout manager: PATCH /api/rollouts/{route}/fallback -> model: rdl-7b-ql-100.
  5) If KV cache miss storm detected: pause cache TTL evaporation job and increase TTL for hot prefixes.
  6) If kernel / runtime error: collect core logs (/var/log/serving-runtime/*.log), gdb dump if needed, and escalate to runtime-team.

Runbook: Node or GPU OOM / eviction
- Pager: infra-platform.
- Steps:
  1) Mark node unschedulable: kubectl cordon <node>
  2) Drain low-priority pods and trigger pod reschedule: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
  3) If GPU driver crash, restart nvidia-container-toolkit and kubelet and monitor dmesg for OOM messages.
  4) Replace node if instability persists; follow cloud provider flow for instance replacement.

Escalation matrix (summary)
- SEV3: Notify Slack #platform-ops, assignee oncall + 1 IC owner.
- SEV2: Page oncall rotation and notify ENG-DL + product manager.
- SEV1: All-hands page and immediate exec notification; fallback policies enabled; incident commander appointed.

4) Retrospective highlights (Q1 2026)

Summary: Q1 brought two high-severity incidents that exposed capacity and routing gaps. The team triaged and closed action items; notable outcomes include:
- Incident A (2026-01-18): Region failover delay caused 12 minutes of elevated latency for EU customers. Root cause: DNS TTLs and a slow healthcheck loop. Action: lowered DNS TTLs to 30s for critical routes; added a fast healthcheck path.
- Incident B (2026-02-03): Cache eviction storm after a model rollout caused p99 latency spikes. Root cause: rollout changed request distribution which caused hot-prefix churn. Action: rollout policy updated to warm prefixes during canary (see rollout manager playbook); increased default prefix TTL.

Lessons learnt and actions completed:
- Improve deploy-time load testing (completed): CI now runs a lightweight traffic simulation for the top 10 production routes.
- Add per-route circuit breakers (in progress): design doc merged; implementation planned for Q2.
- Observability gaps filled (completed): added p99 per-model variant panels and request-id tracing links in Grafana.

Open action items (owner / ETA):
- Per-route canary warming (serving-runtime) / owner: Jonah Reed / ETA: 2026-04-15
- Autoscale policy tuning (infra-platform) / owner: Maya Fernández / ETA: 2026-05-01
- Chaos test for DNS failover (eng-sre) / owner: Derek Liu / ETA: 2026-06-01

5) Roadmap (Q2–Q3 2026): priorities and milestones

Q2 2026 (near-term):
- Implement per-route circuit breakers and rollout warmup (priority P0).
- Autoscale policy improvements: cooldown heuristics and burst capacity adjustments (P0).
- Alert refinement: reduce noisey alerts by adding rate thresholds and service-level filters (P1).
- Dashboard refresh: consolidate per-pool GPU panels and add cost-per-token breakdown (P1).

Q3 2026 (mid-term):
- Smart routing enhancements: latency-aware multi-variant routing and automated fallbacks (P0).
- Cost optimization: adaptive batching policy which tunes batch windows by workload (P1).
- Private deployment observability bundle: packaged dashboards, alert rules, and onprem runbooks for customers (P1).

6) Ownership & run cadence

- Oncall rotations: channeled by service (api-gateway, serving-runtime, infra-platform). Primary oncall schedule maintained in PagerDuty.
- Run cadence: weekly oncall sync (30m), monthly platform reliability review, and quarterly roadmap review with product.
- Meeting artifacts: RETRO notes, action items tracked in JIRA with \"Platform-OPS\" label.

7) Appendix: useful commands, links and templates

Common CLI snippets
- Rollback last api-gateway deployment:
  kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/api-gateway
- Scale GPU pool (internal API):
  curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://controlplane.internal/api/pools/general/scale -d '{"replicas": 8}'
- Query p99 latency in Prometheus:
  curl -g 'http://prometheus.internal/api/v1/query?query=histogram_quantile(0.99,%20sum(rate(serving_latency_seconds_bucket[5m]))%20by%20(le,model_variant))'

Links (internal)
- Platform runbooks index: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-systems-services-playbook-2026-q1.json
- Rollout manager design: /confluence/eng-platform/serving-runtime-runtime-architecture.json#rollout-manager
- Incident retrospectives: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems/

Template: Post-incident actions (to add to JIRA)
- Title: <Incident short title> — <YYYY-MM-DD>
- Summary: 1–2 sentences
- Timeline: bullet list timestamps
- Root cause: single-line summary + evidence
- Remediation: immediate and long-term actions, owners, ETA
- Follow-ups: monitoring and test coverage to prevent regression

Diagram (described)
- The Overview diagram shows API requests entering api-gateway -> request-router -> selection of serving-runtime pool -> optional KV-cache hit -> immediate response or batch scheduling. In failover, the router will fallback to a lower-cost model variant in another region.
